title: The Ecosystem Upkeep Fee is levied on an Agent's market capitalization, not its revenue or profit
content:
A.2.2.7.1 sets the Ecosystem Upkeep Fee at "an annual fee equivalent to 50 basis points (bps) (0.50%) of their market capitalization to Sky, payable in USDS and accounted for monthly," divided into twelve equal monthly payments due on the first day of each month.

The choice of base is the design decision, not the rate. Charging on **market capitalization** rather than revenue, assets under management, or profit produces distinctive incentives. The fee is owed by an Agent with no income; it scales with market enthusiasm rather than economic activity; and success in raising an Agent's token price directly raises its obligation to the ecosystem. It is closer to a property tax on claimed value than a share of output.

A.2.2.7.1.2 defines valuation as total token supply multiplied by the token's TWAP over the 24 hours ending 23:59 UTC on the last day of the month. The TWAP window is anti-manipulation machinery: a point-in-time price on payment day would invite suppressing the token for a few minutes each month. Using *total* supply rather than circulating supply also removes the alternative dodge of parking supply outside the count.

The fee is payable in USDS, which quietly makes every Prime Agent a structural source of demand for Sky's own stablecoin. And A.2.2.7.1.1 leaves the destination address "specified in a future iteration of the Atlas" — the obligation is fully calibrated while its payment rail is not yet named.
description: 50bps annually, split into twelve monthly USDS payments, valued by 24-hour TWAP of total supply — so the fee tracks market valuation and is owed regardless of income.
